title: Model 1 — obligation register entry
description: One legal or regulatory obligation, decomposed into the lifecycle stages that must carry it. The register is the jurisdiction-specific layer: the lifecycle stays generic, and obligations are added, amended or retired here without altering the model.

criterion.description: The question the admissibility gate must ask before execution proceeds.

failure_outcome.description: What the gate returns when the criterion is not met.

validity.description: For criteria satisfied by an instrument that expires. A criterion met once and never re-checked is the quietest failure in a register: it was true, nobody changed anything, and it stopped being true.

monitored_by.description: The control that watches the expiry. Absent, the criterion is unwatched.

type.description: A disclosure implemented in an interface is a design control; one implemented in a manual is procedural. They fail differently and are evidenced differently.

record.description: The record that demonstrates the control operated.

generated_at.description: When the record comes into existence. Records that can only be generated on demand are the weakest kind: they are reconstructions.

retention.description: Retention requirement or reference to the governing schedule.

instrument.description: The instrument, by its formal designation.

provision.description: The specific article, clause or principle. One entry per provision: sub-provisions of the same article often bind different parties and land on different stages.

jurisdiction.description: Territorial scope as it applies in practice, including extraterritorial reach where the instrument has it.

bearer.description: Who carries the duty — provider, deployer, controller, operator, accountable authority. Getting this wrong is the most common register error, because it determines which organisation's gate the criterion belongs in.

applies_from.description: Date the obligation becomes applicable (ISO 8601). Null where not yet fixed.

status.description: Transitional covers deferred or phased application; the register must be able to hold an obligation that is law but not yet biting. 'Advisory' covers standards and guidance that carry no statutory force but function as a procurement condition or an expected baseline — a register that can only hold statute will miss most of what actually binds an organisation.

summary.description: The duty in the register-keeper's own words. Never the instrument's text — reproducing statutory or standards wording creates a licensing and accuracy liability, and a paraphrase forces the register-keeper to demonstrate they understood it.

decomposition.description: The four columns that connect an obligation to the lifecycle. An entry with an empty array in any column is not necessarily wrong, but it is a finding: something must carry the duty, and if nothing does, the obligation is documented and inert.

gate_criteria.description: Pre-execution conditions. Populated only where the duty must be satisfied before an action proceeds.

assurance_activities.description: Independent confirmation that the controls operated.

related_standards.description: Standards that support conformance. Designations only — no reproduced clause text.

source.description: Where the primary text may be read. The register points; it does not reproduce.

review_date.description: When this entry must next be re-checked against the instrument. An obligation register without review dates decays silently.

duty_character.description: How the duty persists. 'Discharged at design' is satisfied once and stays satisfied until the system changes. 'Standing' can lapse with nobody acting at all — stock arrives, an adjacent use changes, a permit expires — so the gate must be re-entered on triggers rather than only on a proposed action. The gate model assumes an action to authorise; standing duties have none, which is why this field exists.

reentry_triggers.description: Events that return a standing duty to the admissibility gate. Required in substance for standing duties: without them the gate is never re-entered and conformance is asserted from the last check indefinitely.

applicability.description: For obligations that bind only above a threshold or on a condition. Scope can be crossed by ordinary trading, with no decision taken and nobody aware. An obligation not yet binding but capable of becoming so is a real register state and needs somewhere to sit.

condition.description: What brings the organisation into scope.

threshold_basis.description: Where the threshold is defined. Record the reference, not a figure taken from memory — thresholds vary by jurisdiction and schedule, and a wrong number in a register is worse than none.

monitoring_control.description: The control that watches whether the threshold has been crossed. Absent, scope is unmonitored.

currently_in_scope.description: 'Unknown' is a legitimate and reportable state.

latent_exposure.description: For anticipatory obligations, where the duty crystallises in the future but the harm begins now. The ordinary fields cannot express this: applies_from says when a duty starts, and has no way to say that action was required well before it. The canonical case is harvest-now-decrypt-later, where data exfiltrated today is decrypted when a capability arrives that does not yet exist.

harm_begins.description: 'On collection' is the inverted case: exposure accrues from the moment data exists, and no later control can undo it.

confidentiality_horizon_years.description: How long the asset must remain confidential. Usually set by a retention schedule or a statutory secrecy period — a number the organisation already knows and rarely connects to this.

migration_duration_years.description: Realistic elapsed time to complete mitigation across the estate, including discovery and vendor dependencies.

capability_horizon_years.description: Estimated time until the capability that realises the harm exists. Genuinely uncertain, and the entry should record the assumption rather than pretend to knowledge.

mitigation_must_start_by.description: The date derived by working backwards from the capability horizon by the migration duration. This is the field that turns an anticipatory obligation into a present decision — the same move the admissibility gate makes for actions.

basis.description: How the dates were derived, so a reviewer can test the assumption rather than the conclusion.

depends_on.description: Dependencies on other register entries. Two obligations can each look adequately carried while the combination is impossible — most often because one is mitigated by a control the other constrains. Recording the dependency is what makes a framework of frameworks structurally true rather than presentational: the connectedness becomes checkable.

entry_id.description: The id of the entry depended on. Must resolve within the register.

nature.description: 'Mitigation gated by' is the constraining case: this duty cannot be discharged faster than the entry it depends on permits.

note.description: What specifically is constrained, and by what.

contingent_on.description: For dates or duties that are agreed but not yet law. Between political agreement and publication in the official gazette there is a real interval in which commentary, official guidance and even the regulator's own timeline pages may all report different states of the world. 'Status: transitional' cannot express this: a provisional agreement is not a transitional provision. Records what must happen before the entry's dates bind.

condition.description: What must occur — publication in the official journal or gazette, commencement proclamation, adoption of an implementing act.

expected_by.description: When the condition is expected to be met (ISO 8601). Set the review date at or before this.

resolved.description: True once the condition is met. An entry left contingent after its expected date is stale by definition.

resolved_by.description: The instrument or event that resolved it, with a citation.
